title: Britain and its colonies switch to the Gregorian calendar
summary: Across Great Britain and its American colonies, Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed directly by Thursday 14 September. Eleven days were dropped and the legal year now began on 1 January.
reason: Britain had kept the Julian calendar long after most of Catholic Europe, which made dates in trade and diplomacy confusing.
significance: It aligned the English speaking world with the calendar most of the world uses today.
